newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Rainbow Chicken to pare year loss.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Rainbow Chicken to pare year loss.

text.p: Rebounding chicken prices and stable second half costs are expected to help pare Rainbow Chicken Ltd's full year loss by about a third, analysts said on Friday.
"Over the first half what really squeezed them was oversupply in the industry and the price came down and they had that feed price inflation," Investec analyst Carolyn Windsor told Reuters.
"In the second half, the prices moved ahead quite nicely for broilers," she added.
Rainbow is expected to release its results for the year to March 31 on Thursday.
Analysts on average forecast a contraction in Rainbow's pre-exceptional losses to 27.8 cents a share from 43.4 cents a share a year ago. The firm was expected to continue not paying a dividend.

But they said company, a unit of Hunt Leuchars & Hepburn Holdings Ltd, had made accurate forecasting difficult by keeping tight-lipped since the appointment of its new managing director Jorge Antonio Corral Ibarrondo in November.
"It's really a thumbsuck. They won't speak to any analysts," said one.
Analysts said Rainbow's second half would benefit from a higher average chicken price of about eight rand a kilogram from an average of 6.50 rand to seven rand for the first half.
"(Prices) were depressed pretty much up until August," said Investec's Windsor.

She added Rainbow was also likely to have built in some provisioning in its reported first half loss of 44.6 cents a share, buffering it against some of its ongoing operational woes in the second half.
Analysts forecast Rainbow would continue to trim its losses and possibly break even by the end of fiscal 1997/98.

With bird prices and feed costs likely to be stable to slightly better over the short term, the firm's fortunes in the current year depended on it turning around operating factors such as feed conversion and mortality rates, they said.
Analysts were keen to see what effect the new Rainbow chief would have on the company's performance.
"I would really expect him to start making his mark in the current financial year," said Windsor.
